text: The impediment to action advances action. What stands in the way becomes the way.

text: Waste no more time arguing about what a good man should be. Be one.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: If it is not right, do not do it; if it is not true, do not say it.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: The best revenge is not to be like your enemy.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Loss is nothing else but change, and change is Nature's delight.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: How much more grievous are the consequences of anger than the causes of it.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Never esteem anything as of advantage to you that will make you break your word or lose your self-respect.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Do every act of your life as though it were the very last act of your life.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: You have power over your mind, not outside events. Realize this, and you will find strength.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Very little is needed to make a happy life; it is all within yourself, in your way of thinking.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Accept the things to which fate binds you, and love the people with whom fate brings you together.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: The object of life is not to be on the side of the majority, but to escape finding oneself in the ranks of the insane.

text: It is not death that a man should fear, but he should fear never beginning to live.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: The happiness of your life depends upon the quality of your thoughts.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: When you wake up in the morning, tell yourself: the people I deal with today will be meddling, ungrateful, arrogant, dishonest, jealous and surly. They are like this because they cannot tell good from evil. But I have seen the beauty of good, and the ugliness of evil, and have recognized that the wrongdoer has a nature related to my own.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Look back over the past, with its changing empires that rose and fell, and you can foresee the future too. Its pattern will be the same, deviating only in minor details. And to watch the mortal life of one man is to see them all.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Almost nothing material is needed for a happy life, for he who has understood existence.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Make the best use of what is in your power, and take the rest as it happens.

text: No man is free who is not master of himself.
author: Epictetus

text: First say to yourself what you would be; and then do what you have to do.

text: If you want to improve, be content to be thought foolish and stupid with regard to external things.

text: Freedom is not procured by a full enjoyment of what is desired, but by controlling the desire.

text: People are disturbed not by things, but by the views which they take of things.
author: Epictetus

text: Seek not the good in external things; seek it in yourself.

text: Never say about anything that I have lost it; but only that I have given it back.

text: Seek not for the things which happen as you wish; but wish the things which happen to be as they are, and you will have a tranquil life.

text: Wealth consists not in having great possessions, but in having few wants.

text: He is a wise man who does not grieve for the things which he has not, but rejoices for those which he has.
author: Epictetus

text: Don't explain your philosophy. Embody it.

text: We cannot choose our external circumstances, but we can always choose how we respond to them.
author: Epictetus

text: First learn the meaning of what you say, and then speak.

text: You become what you give your attention to. If you yourself don't choose what thoughts and images you expose yourself to, someone else will.

text: There is only one way to happiness and that is to cease worrying about things which are beyond the power of our will.
author: Epictetus

text: All things are foreign to us; time alone is ours.
author: Seneca

text: While we are postponing, life speeds by.
author: Seneca

text: It is not the man who has too little, but the man who craves more, that is poor.
author: Seneca

text: Begin at once to live, and count each separate day as a separate life.
author: Seneca

text: The greatest obstacle to living is expectancy, which hangs upon tomorrow and loses today.

source: On the Shortness of Life, IX

text: No man was ever wise by chance.
author: Seneca

text: Retire into yourself as much as you can; associate with those who are likely to improve you.
author: Seneca

text: A happy life is one which is in accordance with its own nature.

text: If you wish to be loved, love.
author: Seneca

text: We suffer more often in imagination than in reality.
author: Seneca

text: One who is everywhere is nowhere.
author: Seneca

text: To live is to fight.
author: Seneca

text: Luck is what happens when preparation meets opportunity.
author: Seneca

text: True happiness is to enjoy the present, without anxious dependence upon the future, not to amuse ourselves with either hopes or fears but to rest satisfied with what we have, which is sufficient.

text: Better to trip with the feet than with the tongue.
author: Zeno of Citium

text: The goal of life is to live in agreement with Nature.

text: We have two ears and one mouth, so that we should listen more than we say.
author: Zeno of Citium

text: Man conquers the world by conquering himself.
author: Zeno of Citium

text: All the good are friends of one another.
author: Zeno of Citium

text: Lead me, Zeus, lead me, Destiny, wherever I have been assigned by you. I will follow without hesitation; and if I am unwilling, because I am wicked, I will follow nonetheless.

text: All things are parts of one single system, which is called Nature; the individual life is good when it is in harmony with Nature.
author: Cleanthes

text: Practice yourself in little things, and thence proceed to greater.
author: Cleanthes

text: If you accomplish something good with hard work, the labor passes quickly, but the good endures; if you do something shameful in pursuit of pleasure, the pleasure passes quickly, but the shame endures.
author: Musonius Rufus

text: We must not say that it befits only the philosopher to inquire how one ought to live rightly; for philosophy is nothing else than this — the inquiry into what is fitting and appropriate for a human being.
author: Musonius Rufus

text: Choose to die well while you can; wait too long, and it might become impossible to do so.
author: Musonius Rufus

text: The man who is truly good and wise neither struggles with adversity nor complains of his lot; rather, he takes heart from even the harshest of conditions.
author: Musonius Rufus

text: The philosopher's aim is not to hear many lectures and then fall silent, but to live by those already heard.
author: Musonius Rufus

text: If I had followed the multitude, I would not have studied philosophy.
author: Chrysippus

text: The virtues are interconnected; whoever truly possesses one virtue possesses them all.
author: Chrysippus

text: No one is born a sage; goodness is an art which must be learned.
author: Chrysippus

text: The universe is change; our life is what our thoughts make it.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Dwell on the beauty of life. Watch the stars, and see yourself running with them.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: The art of living is more like wrestling than dancing.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Everything is but what your opinion makes it; and that opinion lies with yourself.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Adapt yourself to the things with which your lot has been cast.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Confine yourself to the present.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Dig within. There lies the well-spring of good: ever dig, and it will ever flow.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Such as are thy habitual thoughts, such also will be the character of thy mind.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Difficulties are things that show a person what they are.

text: Only the educated are free.
author: Epictetus

text: Know first who you are, and then adorn yourself accordingly.
author: Epictetus

text: If you wish to be a writer, write; if you wish to be a reader, read.
author: Epictetus

text: When you close your doors and make darkness within, remember never to say that you are alone, for you are not alone.

text: Lameness is an impediment to the leg, but not to the will.

text: It is impossible for a man to learn what he thinks he already knows.

text: It is not because things are difficult that we do not dare; it is because we do not dare that they are difficult.

text: Difficulties strengthen the mind, as labor does the body.

text: There is no easy way from the earth to the stars.

text: He suffers more than necessary, who suffers before it is necessary.
author: Seneca

text: Wherever there is a human being, there is an opportunity for kindness.
author: Seneca

text: If one does not know to which port one is sailing, no wind is favorable.
author: Seneca

text: The day which we fear as our last is but the birthday of eternity.
author: Seneca

text: The most necessary part of philosophy is that which is put into practice.

text: Will not the educated woman be sensible? Yes; will not she be just? Of course.

text: No man steps in the same river twice.

text: Character is destiny.
author: Heraclitus

text: The sun is new each day.
author: Heraclitus

text: I am a citizen of the world.

author: Diogenes the Cynic

text: It is a royal thing to do good and be reviled.

source: Plutarch, Life of Cato the Younger

text: We are each the center of a series of concentric circles — self, family, neighbors, fellow citizens, humanity. The work is to draw the outer circles toward the center.

text: Reject your sense of injury, and the injury itself disappears.

text: Be like the rocky promontory against which the restless surf continually pounds.

text: Whatever happens to you has been waiting to happen since the beginning of time.

text: Time is a river of passing events; strong is its current.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Do not act as if you had ten thousand years to live.

text: How much trouble he avoids who does not look to see what his neighbor says or does.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Begin — to begin is half the work; let half still remain. Begin again, and thou wilt have finished.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: It is the act of an ill-instructed man to blame others; of one whose instruction is beginning, to blame himself; of one whose instruction is complete, to blame neither.

text: All philosophy lies in two words: sustain and abstain.

text: Don't let the force of an impression when it first hits you knock you off your feet.

text: Let us prepare our minds as if we had come to the very end of life.
author: Seneca
